Pipeline stage: simulate a computerized adaptive test

Source: R/pipeline-forms.R
simulate_cat.Rd

Simulates a computerized adaptive test (CAT) from the calibrated items with mirtCAT, to see how precise, how long and how secure the test would be before it goes live. Simulees are drawn from a standard normal ability distribution on the bank scale (or given in theta); each takes a CAT that starts with the most informative item, picks items by maximum information (criteria), estimates ability by method, and stops when the standard error reaches min_sem or max_items items are given.

Usage

simulate_cat(
  p,
  n = 1000,
  min_sem = NULL,
  max_items = 30,
  min_items = 5,
  criteria = "MI",
  method = "MAP",
  randomesque = 1,
  theta = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

p

a calibrated pipeline from calibrate().

n

number of simulees.

min_sem

standard error at which the CAT stops. Defaults to the cat_sem rule.

max_items, min_items

longest and shortest test.

criteria

item selection criterion passed to mirtCAT::mirtCAT().

method

ability estimation method passed to mirtCAT::mirtCAT().

randomesque

exposure control: choose each item at random from the randomesque most informative ones (1 means none).

theta

optional true abilities of the simulees.

seed

optional random seed.

Value

The pipeline with p$forms (a list with method = "cat", persons, a tibble with each simulee's true and estimated ability, standard error and test length, exposure, a tibble of item exposure rates, and summary).

Details

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • cat_precision (review): the average final standard error is above cat_sem, or the average bias of the ability estimates is beyond cat_bias in absolute value.

  • cat_exposure (review): an item is given to more than max_exposure of the simulees. Use randomesque to spread exposure.

  • unused_items (review): more than unused_share of the bank is never used.

  • bank_depth (info): the bank holds fewer than bank_depth times max_items items.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mirtCAT", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- add_responses(mv_pipeline(), certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key)
  p <- calibrate(drop_items(p, "Q14"), model = "2PL")
  p <- simulate_cat(p, n = 200, max_items = 15, seed = 1)
  p$forms$summary
}
